findings.failure_path: startswith anchors only the candidate's start; an author can append @@ hunks continuing the last file's diff (or a reverting diff) that a packet-bounded reviewer cannot distinguish from candidate content, so a dangerous change reads as reverted or harmless while the receipt binds the un-reverted candidate and the merge-side binder accepts it
findings.smallest_fix: disclose the candidate extent to the reviewer: record the candidate byte length in the review profile and state that exactly the first N packet bytes land, or require and gate-verify a fixed end-of-candidate sentinel line immediately after the prefix

concern_results.conclusion: Prefix anchoring blocks prepended decoys, truncation, interleaving, empty candidates, and --paths without --base; the chain/succession relaxations compare candidate-to-candidate and accept only the widened shape the gate itself produces; the open bypass is the unanchored back edge: startswith fixes where the candidate starts but nothing delimits where it ends, so trailing bytes continuing diff grammar (extra @@ hunks on the last file, or a reverting diff) blend into the candidate for a packet-bounded reviewer and read as part of the change, matching the exact decoy class the prefix anchor was added to kill

Containment evidence is genuinely discriminating (identity-collapse and anchor-removal mutants red exactly their owning cases, the non-discriminating binder mutation is honestly recorded, combined wording-only refusal fails closed), but the enforced property only proves the reviewer was shown the landing bytes, not that the reviewer can tell landing bytes from appended context, and the register/contract claim "the reviewer knows which part is the change" is asserted without any mechanism that makes it true

challenge_focus: Attack the prefix anchor and the two-object split. The packet must BEGIN with the base-derived candidate. Find a packet satisfying startswith that still misleads a reviewer about what lands -- trailing content reading as the real change, a second candidate copy, or context resupplying a dropped hunk. The chain compares candidate to candidate, not packet to packet: construct a round sequence this permits whose combined evidence misrepresents what any single reviewer saw. Inspect the relaxations in _validate_chain_succession and the in-chain prior-receipt checks for a receipt shape now wrongly accepted. Can candidate_paths taken from the candidate under-select an owner? Probe the empty-candidate guard, --paths without --base, and the combined-form wording-only refusal. Check whether the register rows overstate what the mutations established.
